names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 1 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Ακάκιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας», with the rank word left off. Its life page gives «Ακάκιος ή Άσιος», Acacius or Asius, as two forms of the one name.
The alternative form saint.gr prints on his life page: «Ο Άγιος Ιερομάρτυρας Ακάκιος ή Άσιος ήταν διάκονος».

death.note: saint.gr: «μαρτύρησε στη Γαλλία το 303 μ.Χ., επί αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού (284-305 μ.Χ.)», and the page heads him «(; - 303)». No year of birth is printed.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Ακάκιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 1 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and the whole of it is one sentence: «Ο Άγιος Ιερομάρτυρας Ακάκιος ή Άσιος ήταν διάκονος και μαρτύρησε στη Γαλλία το 303 μ.Χ., επί αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού (284-305 μ.Χ.).» **He is not the other Acacius of this day**: the same 1 Μαΐου listing carries «Άγιοι Ακάκιος ο Οσιομάρτυρας από το Νεοχώρι Θεσσαλονίκης...», who is the corpus's `acacius-the-new-of-neochorion`, beheaded at Constantinople in 1816 — two entries on one calendar day are two commemorations and these two are plainly two men, a deacon under Diocletian and a monk under the Ottomans. The corpus's other Acacii are of Melitene, of Latros, of Tver, the centurion, the obedient and one of the Forty, none of them a deacon in Gaul. **The display name keeps the page's alternative form** because the bare Acacius would not tell him from six others, and the see and the epithet he has none of; the rank is left to `types`. His companion Acelus is the one `related` row, on the strength of the other page's own words. No hymn, no relic, no place in Gaul named.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
